summary: M1 re-verified after rebuild #2 of both steps. Verdict ready-with-findings. Both steps documented; 43 references examined - 10 resolve in M1, 28 are standard and pre-existing, 5 unclassifiable in-tree (F-02), 0 unresolved; the two step manifests merged into reports/MILESTONE-M1-package.xml with no version conflict and no member collision, and its two BusinessProcess members changed to the stem form; both executable milestone tests exit 0, the checker now with 0 findings where v1 had 2; an observation-only run of check_case_management_setup.py exits 0. F-09, F-10 and F-11 are CLOSED at the skill and proven three ways including negative controls this run; F-07 is closed by the artefacts. F-01 through F-06 and F-08 remain open, and F-01's remedy pointer is corrected from M2-S01 to M2-S03 - a stale pointer the v1 report and two unrewritable gate notes carry. Three new findings: F-12 (set-milestone moved M1 accepted -> verified with no guard while the gate record still reads approved), F-13 (the merged manifest has never been read by a deploy and its CompactLayout member form is disputed by the only deploy run), F-14 (record-type-decision.md still names the pre-rebuild process spellings and is what manual line 1 sends a human to read). Five manual lines remain the human's; no gate approved, no org contacted.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 rubric. Every step was documented, the merged manifest built with no conflict, and every declared acceptance test existed and ran, which would support HIGH. MEDIUM because the reference class this milestone exists to close was still not fully classifiable: the record-type-to-layout binding had zero references to resolve (F-01) and the five business-process Status references resolve only outside the tree (F-02). Two things deliberately did not raise it: the 12/12 org validation is external corroboration the rubric does not score, and the two exit-0 checker runs were only treated as meaningful after negative controls showed the new rules fire.

dimensions_skipped.reason: Five of the six reference classes in the Step 3 table had zero references because their metadata belongs to later milestones (ValidationRule M3-S01; AssignmentRules M3-S03/S04; Flow and EntitlementProcess M4; and M2-S01's PermissionSet grants a custom permission with no object or field permissions). The sixth resolved 10 of 10 in-tree references but could not classify the five business-process Status values, which resolve only against the target org's CaseStatus (A28, F-02).
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Re-run reference resolution at the M2 milestone, once M2-S03's profiles carry layoutAssignments and M2-S02's carry recordTypeVisibilities and fieldPermissions.

findings.title: The record-type to layout binding is asserted nowhere in M1, and v1's remedy pointer named the wrong step
findings.detail: check_record_type_layouts.py resolves every record-type-to-layout check from layoutAssignments, and collect() populates them only from Profile and PermissionSet roots. No Profile exists anywhere under artefacts/. The build-scoped run is still the byte-for-byte union of the two step-scoped runs and adds no assertion neither made. It is sharper evidence than v1's: the 8th file it now sweeps IS a PermissionSet (M2-S01's Case_Intake_Integration), one of the two roots collect() reads, and it still resolves zero layoutAssignments because that permission set carries a customPermissions grant and nothing else. CORRECTION OF RECORD: v1 said layoutAssignments is M2-S01's; in plan v5 it is M2-S03's ('Minimal base profiles carrying only default app, default record type and layout assignment'). The stale pointer was copied into two human_gates notes (milestone:M1 and step:M2-S01) which no agent may rewrite.
findings.recommendation: v6: reword the milestone test description to what the run proves, and move the record-type-to-layout binding assertion onto an M2 milestone test at --manifest-dir artefacts once M2-S03's profiles exist. The two gate notes are not rewritable; this report is the correction of record.

findings.title: set-milestone overwrites an accepted milestone with no guard, and this run triggered it
findings.detail: scripts/build_plan.py protects a human's G3 in one place and not the other. set-status <step> running leaves an accepted milestone alone - its guard set is {pending, rejected, verified} and its comment reads 'only the human undoes their own G3'. cmd_set_milestone assigns milestone['status'] unconditionally. AGENT.md Step 9 requires this agent to record its verdict with set-milestone, so milestones[M1].status has moved accepted -> verified while human_gates[milestone:M1].status remains approved. The two records now disagree and only a human can reconcile them, because no agent writes a gate.

findings.title: The merged milestone manifest has never been read by a deploy, and its CompactLayout member is spelled differently by the only tool that has ever named it

Both mock deploys ran --source-dir force-app --dry-run, so the CLI derived components from the source tree and never opened a package.xml - and what it derived was the object-qualified 'CompactLayout Case.Case_Intake'. The build's manifest says one thing, the only deploy ever run said another, and nothing has compared them. The always-on manifest test cannot catch it: it checks the manifest against the files in the build and both sides agree with each other. Milestone-level form of decisions.md O-M1S01-03.
findings.recommendation: Human, optional and outside this loop: run sf project deploy start --manifest reports/MILESTONE-M1-package.xml --dry-run --target-org <sandbox> once, or retrieve to see the member form the org emits. No agent in this loop contacts an org.

process_observations.observation: The loop did the thing it exists to do: a defect reality found became library content and then a checker, and the rebuild was gated by that checker rather than by a human remembering. Three HIGH findings closed at the source in four days, and the rebuilt artefacts validated unmodified.

Both new rule families were verified against reverted fixtures before their exit-0 was reported as meaning anything. The step tester had already run the same negative control on CMS-STEM-01/02, which is the discipline F-01 exists to teach - a silent checker reads as a clean one.

build-doc-keeper recorded the divergence between the accepted milestone and the rebuilt artefacts, named who may and may not fix each part, and sequenced the re-verification so it would run once rather than twice - including a warning that two sessions were writing this build directory concurrently.

Fixes land forward but do not reach back. F-04 (deploy-order.md undeclared) and F-08 (production deploy command against a sandbox alias) are both correct on M2-S01 and both still wrong on the two M1 steps - and F-08's two files were rewritten during rebuild #2 without being revisited. A rebuild re-runs the builder; it does not re-open findings filed against what the builder wrote last time.

The CLI guards a human's G3 in set-status and not in set-milestone, so an agent following its own prescribed Step 9 moved an accepted milestone back to verified. The asymmetry is in one file, twenty lines apart, and the guarded branch even carries the comment explaining why the guard exists.
